A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, retitled in v4. Their complete texts, equations, figure and table are readable. The datasets and applications material in v4's appendix can be matched to v3's main text.

before.justification: Section 3 explicitly states that the authors calculate mean or median dataset statistics when these are unavailable from sources, with descriptive summaries reported in Table 1. This constitutes original data analysis, although no model experiments are presented.

after.justification: Table 1 retains the descriptive dataset statistics whose author calculations are documented in v3, including unchanged mean/median entries. These retained data-analysis results qualify, although v4 omits the calculation explanation and presents no model experiments.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a prediction algorithm or model. Added method descriptions and taxonomy revisions concern the organization of cited research, rather than changes to a proposed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands from 21 to 28 catalogued datasets, but neither version reports using these datasets for model training or evaluation. The expansion concerns surveyed resources rather than experimental task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed algorithm. Newly discussed methods such as MSPred, MAL and VideoPoet expand the literature review, not an experimentally evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Neither version reports a model-evaluation protocol. The added discussion of pixel losses and classifier-based perceptual metrics describes practices in the literature, without introducing or revising an evaluation conducted by this work.

E4.justification: Neither PDF presents ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity tests or empirical case studies. The new tokenizer-limitations discussion is explanatory analysis, without accompanying experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean/median reporting convention, including for added rows. Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The removed explanation concerns the provenance of dataset summaries rather than a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds seven quantitative dataset summaries. Examples include D2-City with 11,211 videos and 750 mean frames, and Kinetics-700 with 650,000 videos and 250 mean frames. All 21 retained dataset rows preserve their numerical values; these additions are descriptive statistics rather than prediction-performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 retains Equation (1) and adds Equation (2), extending the formal conditioning variables to auxiliary observations and future user-control signals. This is a limited extension of the mathematical problem definition; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central stochasticity-based taxonomy and prediction-generation integration claim remain. The taxonomy contribution is refined by reclassifying optical flow under raw-pixel methods, adding depth under feature methods, and replacing the unguided/text-guided generative split with diffusion-based/token-based categories.

C2.justification: V4 newly explains how visual-tokenizer reconstruction requirements and finite language-model context windows constrain long-video modeling. It also adds challenges in integrating optical flow with synthesis quality and long-term generation. The broader limitations concerning generalization, stochasticity and computational demands remain.

D1.justification: V3 Section 3 explains that missing dataset properties are calculated using means or medians. V4 removes this explanation from both the main text and appendix while retaining the table's statistical markers, reducing provenance information for reproducing the dataset summaries.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands coverage of visual tokenizers and language-model-based generation, including MAGVIT-v2, VideoPoet, Painter and SegGPT, and explicitly positions the survey against earlier reviews. Thirty cited works are added and three removed: VideoGPT, Kolors and the continuous-process CVP paper. Additional coverage includes depth prediction and optical-flow research.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change throughout from video prediction to future frame synthesis. Section 6 is substantially reorganized and expanded around diffusion and token mechanisms, optical-flow discussion changes subsections, and dataset/application material is reorganized into appendix Sections 9–10.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, relabelled and revised to reflect the changed taxonomy, moving from page 1 to page 2. Table 1 retains its columns but gains seven rows and moves from page 4 to page 9 near the appendix. The overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: V4 provides a clearer account of generative approaches through Section 6's diffusion/token organization and its new explanation of tokenizer and context-window bottlenecks. Explicit positioning against prior surveys also clarifies the contribution. These gains outweigh the limited transparency loss from removing the dataset-statistics calculation note, while the central thesis remains stable.
